eyebrow: Zero Trust Implementation & Security Engineering Capstone · Chapter 1
subtitle: Lesson 1 · Zero Trust Principles

steps.label: Owned Network
steps.sub: Enterprise controlled the switches, WAN, and data center

steps.label: Managed Devices
steps.sub: Anything on the LAN was assumed to be an IT-imaged machine

steps.label: One-Time Login
steps.sub: VPN or domain logon treated as ongoing proof of trust

steps.label: Cloud & SaaS
steps.sub: Resources moved outside any single network boundary

steps.label: Remote Work
steps.sub: Default user location became "off the corporate LAN"

steps.label: Lateral Movement
steps.sub: Implicit trust inside let one breach reach everything

code:
Perimeter model:
  network location == trust
  inside the firewall  == trusted
  outside the firewall == untrusted

NIST SP 800-207's starting premise:
  resources no longer sit inside one boundary
  so location-based trust can't protect them
caption: Zero Trust doesn't retire the firewall — it retires location as the basis for trust.

subtitle: The seven real tenets SP 800-207 proposes in place of location-based trust.
